  About the project
  Bath Store and More is a Dublin-based bathroom design and installation company helping homeowners transform their bathrooms into luxury spaces. The business needed a professional website to showcase their portfolio, share brochures, highlight showrooms, and make it easy for customers to get a quote.
  This was my second WordPress and Elementor Pro build. Having gone through the learning curve with VIP Ireland, the process was noticeably smoother. I was more confident in the platform, faster with the layout tools, and better at making design decisions from the start.





  What I built
  
    
      Pages
      Home, Portfolio, About, Brochures, Showrooms, Contact, Blogs
    
    
      Tools used
      WordPress, Elementor Pro, custom CSS
    
    
      Focus areas
      Portfolio presentation, brochure downloads, quote request flow, mobile responsiveness
    
    
      Outcome
      Fully live professional website at bathstoreandmore.ie
    
  





  Reflection
  Compared to VIP Ireland, this project felt like a different experience entirely. The foundational knowledge I had built on the first site meant I could focus more on design quality and less on figuring out the tools. The result is a richer, more visual site with a stronger layout and better overall user experience.
  Building two client sites back to back gave me a real sense of progression. I can see the improvement between the two projects and it has given me confidence to take on more complex web design work going forward.




Visit bathstoreandmore.ie

text:

title: Superdry strategic analysis
text:
Strategic data visualisation
The radar chart below maps the competitive intensity of each of Porter’s Five Forces acting on Superdry, scored from 1 (low) to 5 (high) based on our group’s strategic diagnostics.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

labels = ["Competitive\nRivalry", "Supplier\nPower", "Buyer\nPower", "Threat of\nSubstitution", "Threat of\nNew Entry"]
scores = [4, 3, 4, 4, 3]

N = len(labels)
angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, N, endpoint=False)
scores_ext = scores + [scores[0]]
angles_ext = np.append(angles, angles[0])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6), subplot_kw=dict(polar=True))
ax.plot(angles_ext, scores_ext, "o-", linewidth=2, color="#4a90d9")
ax.fill(angles_ext, scores_ext, alpha=0.2, color="#4a90d9")
ax.set_thetagrids(np.degrees(angles), labels, fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylim(0, 5)
ax.set_yticks([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
ax.set_yticklabels(["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"], fontsize=7, color="gray")
ax.set_title("Porter's Five Forces — Superdry", size=12, pad=20, fontweight="bold")
ax.grid(color="gray", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Porter’s Five Forces — Superdry competitive intensity (1 = low, 5 = high)

title: Aleksander Lupa
text:
About me

I'm a final-year Business Studies student at Dublin City University, specialising in Business Analytics. I'm passionate about the point where business questions meet technical problem-solving, using data to clarify what's happening, why it's happening, and what to do next.
My toolkit spans Python (Pandas/NumPy), SQL/MySQL, Power BI/Tableau, Excel, and web fundamentals including HTML/CSS. I also have hands-on experience designing and building multiple websites using WordPress, giving me a practical understanding of how design and content come together for real audiences. I enjoy the full analytical cycle: framing the business problem, building tidy data models, testing assumptions, and communicating insights that drive real decisions.
Outside of work and college, I'm a dedicated bodybuilder. The discipline and consistency that the sport demands carries into everything else I do.

text:
Technology breakdown
The chart below shows an estimated breakdown of time invested across the technologies used to build this site throughout the module.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

technologies = ["SCSS / CSS", "HTML", "Quarto & YAML", "Git & GitHub", "JavaScript", "Python"]
hours = [40, 35, 30, 25, 15, 12]
colors = ["#4a90d9", "#5ba0e0", "#6bb0e7", "#7bc0ee", "#a0d0f5", "#c0e0fb"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
bars = ax.barh(technologies, hours, color=colors, edgecolor="white", height=0.6)

for bar, val in zip(bars, hours):
    ax.text(val + 0.5, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
            f"~{val}h", va="center", fontsize=10)

ax.set_xlabel("Estimated hours invested")
ax.set_title("Time invested by technology — ePortfolio project", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlim(0, 50)
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Estimated hours invested by technology during the ePortfolio project

title: PriceBeo
text:
Financial projections
The chart below visualises PriceBeo’s three-year financial model, comparing projected revenue against startup and operating costs across the growth period.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

years = ["Year 1", "Year 2", "Year 3"]
revenue = [99_440, 312_500, 938_625]
startup = [157_720, 0, 0]
operating = [60_000, 98_000, 210_000]

x = np.arange(len(years))
width = 0.28

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
b1 = ax.bar(x - width, revenue, width, label="Revenue (€)", color="#4a90d9", alpha=0.9)
b2 = ax.bar(x, startup, width, label="Startup Costs (€)", color="#e67e22", alpha=0.9)
b3 = ax.bar(x + width, operating, width, label="Operating Costs (€)", color="#e74c3c", alpha=0.9)

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(years)
ax.set_ylabel("Amount (€)")
ax.set_title("PriceBeo — 3-Year Financial Projections", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend()
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"€{int(v):,}"))
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

for bar in [*b1, *b2, *b3]:
    h = bar.get_height()
    if h > 0:
        ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, h + 4000,
                f"€{int(h):,}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: PriceBeo — projected revenue vs costs over three years

  My fitness journey
  What started as a decision in July 2023 has grown into one of the most disciplined and rewarding parts of my life. My goal is to compete in a men's physique bodybuilding show in 2027. Here is how it has unfolded so far.

The journey



  
    
      July 2023
      The beginning
      Starting out
      Mid-July 2023 I walked into the gym and committed to something new. No experience, no plan beyond showing up. Within weeks training became a non-negotiable part of my routine.
    
    
      
        photo1.jpg
        
      
    
  

  
    
      October 2023
      Cut
      Photoshoot prep
      Just three months in, I committed to a photoshoot prep. I dialled in my nutrition, dropped body fat, and got into the best condition of my life to that point. It proved what was possible with focus and consistency.
    
    
      
        photo2.jpg
        
      
    
  

  
    
      Late 2023 to October 2024
      Bulk
      Year long bulk
      After the photoshoot I went straight into a full year of building. The goal was to add as much quality muscle as possible, eating in a surplus, training hard, and trusting the process over the long term.
    
    
      
        photo3.jpg
        
      
    
  

  
    
      October 2024
      Mini cut
      First mini cut
      After a year of bulking I ran a mini cut to strip back some body fat, tighten up the physique, and assess where the muscle had been added. A short, sharp phase before getting back to building.
    
    
      
        photo4.jpg
        
      
    
  

  
    
      Late 2024 to October 2025
      Bulk
      Second push
      Back into a building phase for another extended push through to October 2025. More structured programming, better understanding of nutrition, and noticeably more size coming into the cut.
    
    
      
        photo5.jpg
        
      
    
  

  
    
      October 2025
      Mini cut
      Second mini cut
      Another mini cut to sharpen up before the next bulk. Each cycle the process gets more refined. Tracking is tighter, the body responds faster, and the result is a cleaner starting point for the next phase.
    
    
      
        photo6.jpg
        
      
    
  

  
    
      January 2026 onwards
      Bulk
      Current phase
      Back in a bulk from January 2026 and building towards the biggest push yet. The 2027 men's physique show is the target and every session, meal, and recovery window is part of that plan.
    
    
      
        photo7.jpg
        
      
    
  



Looking ahead


  The goal: 2027 men's physique show
  Everything I am doing right now is building towards stepping on stage at my first men's physique bodybuilding show in 2027. The cycles of bulking and cutting, the consistency, the discipline around food and training, it all has a single target at the end of it.

The client needed a clean, credible website that communicated the premium nature of the product range and made it easy for potential partners to get in touch.
  This was my first website built entirely from scratch using WordPress and Elementor Pro. I handled everything from the initial setup and theme configuration through to page design, navigation structure, content layout, and mobile responsiveness.

      Focus areas
      Layout design, branding, mobile responsiveness, navigation structure
    
    
      Outcome
      Fully live professional website at vipireland.ie
    
  





  Reflection
  As my first WordPress project, VIP Ireland was a steep but rewarding learning curve. Getting to grips with Elementor Pro, understanding how WordPress themes and plugins interact, and learning to build responsive layouts took time and iteration. By the end of the project I had a solid foundation in the platform and a finished site I was genuinely proud of.
  The experience taught me how to translate a client brief into a real working product, manage the full build process independently, and deliver something polished on a live domain.
